entities.name: Eye of Horus
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian symbol dating back to the Early Dynastic Period (c. 3100–2686 BCE), embodies concepts of protection, royal power, and good health, making it a significant artifact in the study of Egyptian mythology and culture. This symbol, associated with the falcon-headed god Horus, was used extensively in funerary practices and amulets, reflecting the religious beliefs of the ancient Egyptians. Its prominence in artifacts, inscriptions, and temple reliefs across Egypt, particularly in regions such as Thebes and Memphis, highlights its importance in both religious and political contexts.

Historically, the Eye of Horus was believed to possess healing properties and was often invoked for protection in life and the afterlife. The symbol's association with Horus, who avenged his father Osiris, underscored its connotation of justice and protection. The early use of the Eye in the Pyramid Texts (c. 2400–2300 BCE) signifies its deep-rooted presence in Egyptian religious thought. Moreover, the fraction known as the "Eye of Horus" (1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/16 + 1/32 + 1/64) was symbolically used in mathematics, emphasizing the multi-faceted significance of this icon in various aspects of life.

The legacy of the Eye of Horus extends beyond ancient Egypt, influencing various cultures and traditions throughout history. It became a symbol of protection and healing in Greco-Roman contexts and continues to be referenced in modern times, often seen in art, jewelry, and popular culture. The symbol's enduring presence illustrates the cross-cultural transmission of ideas and beliefs, demonstrating how ancient symbols can retain their meanings and adapt through time.
